LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen a long way from its highs, and oddly it's now priced a touch above its bigger defense rivals rather than at its usual discount — but steady military spending means the business itself hasn't changed.

ASML.sentence: ASML dipped a little this week; it looks expensive on today's earnings, but the whole bet rests on their profits ramping up sharply next year as chipmakers keep buying their one-of-a-kind machines.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet and has pulled back a bit off its highs, which is drawing some buying interest — but the business is the usual steady story of selling industrial gases on long contracts and nudging prices up.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm right now, with the big question being whether its Azure cloud keeps growing fast when they report late October — strong cloud numbers would confirm the AI story is still intact.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is steady, and biotech funding has been thawing nicely lately — that money tends to show up in their orders a couple of quarters later, so it's an encouraging backdrop.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge pays a generous dividend and runs its oil and gas pipelines like a toll road, so it's a steady, income-focused holding with nothing dramatic happening.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow is quiet after a sizable pullback, but its long-term contracts are still growing at a healthy clip as big companies and government agencies sign up for its AI workflow tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore had a nice up day, helped by its mining and commodity-trading business, though its earnings look about mid-cycle right now rather than unusually cheap or stretched.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dipped a hair, but the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up — the reported drop is just an accounting quirk from acquisitions, not any real weakness.

KOF.sentence: The Latin American Coca-Cola bottler had a good day, with a steady Mexican peso helping its results translate nicely into dollars.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is steady and oil prices are high, which makes its profits look large right now — but that's a sign it's near the top of the cycle, so it's a moment for a little caution rather than excitement.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is trading for less than its ships would be worth as scrap steel, with the market effectively assigning no value to its logistics business — an unusually cheap price for a bellwether of global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard ticked up and, unusually, is now priced slightly cheaper than its twin Visa rather than at its normal premium, even as people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot company is trading at its steepest discount in years relative to its own history, even though hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines — and each one means more instruments and supplies sold.
